ja: 私はやっと風邪の峠を越えた。
en: I've turned the corner with my cold.
alternatives: My cold has finally started getting better.
I'm finally recovering from my cold.
point: turn the corner は最悪の状態を越えて回復へ向かうこと。

ja: ちょっと熱がある気がします。
en: I might have a fever.
alternatives: I think I have a slight fever.
I might be running a fever.
point: 気がするは I think / may で言い切りを避ける

ja: ここが痛い。
en: It hurts here.
alternatives: This spot hurts.
I feel pain here.
point: hurt は痛むという動詞。

ja: 昨日よりずっと体調がいい。
en: I feel much better than yesterday.
alternatives: I'm feeling a lot better than yesterday.
I feel way better than I did yesterday.
point: better を強めるのは much / a lot。very は不可

ja: 医者曰く、原因はストレスだ。
en: The doctor says stress causes it.
alternatives: The doctor says stress is behind it.
The doctor says it's caused by stress.
point: 「元は〜」は stress causes it や is behind it で言える

ja: 私のは軽症だと、看護師が言った。
en: The nurse said mine was mild.
alternatives: The nurse told me mine wasn't serious.
The nurse said mine isn't serious.
point: said の後ろの節は時制を過去にそろえる

ja: 頭が痛いんだ。
en: I have a headache.
alternatives: My head hurts.
I've got a headache.
point: headache は数えられる名詞なので a

ja: 頭痛に効く薬はありますか？
en: Do you have medicine for headaches?
alternatives: Do you have anything for a headache?
Is there any medicine for headaches?
point: 「〜に効く薬」は medicine for 〜

ja: 痛くてたまらないのは腰なんだ。
en: It's my back that's killing me.
alternatives: My back is what's killing me.
What's killing me is my back.
point: It's ~ that で腰を強調。killing me は痛くてたまらない

ja: 私は歩けるよ。
en: I can walk.
alternatives: I'm able to walk.
I'm capable of walking.
point: can で歩ける能力を伝える。

ja: 彼女は私の発疹はうつらないと言う。
en: She says my rash isn't contagious.
alternatives: She told me my rash isn't contagious.
She says my rash isn't catching.
point: She says の後ろは平叙の節。「うつる」は contagious

ja: 腫れがいつまで続くか分かります？
en: Any idea how long the swelling lasts?
alternatives: Any idea how long the swelling will last?
Do you know how long the swelling lasts?
point: 間接疑問は疑問詞のあとが平叙文の語順

ja: めまいがして、私は座り込んだ。
en: Feeling dizzy, I sat down.
alternatives: Because I felt dizzy, I sat down.
Since I felt dizzy, I sat down.
point: 分詞構文の主語は主節の主語と同じ

ja: 疲れてなければ私は運動するのに。
en: Were I less run-down, I'd exercise.
alternatives: If I weren't worn out, I'd exercise.
I'd work out if I weren't exhausted.
point: Were I は If I were の if を省いた形。

ja: スマホを見るのはやめたんだ。
en: I've quit checking my phone.
alternatives: I stopped checking my phone.
I gave up checking my phone.
point: quit / stop の後は -ing

ja: 私が前兆に対処してたら今は回復期なのに。
en: Had I heeded warning signs, I'd be convalescing.
alternatives: If I'd acted on the warning signs, I'd be recovering.
I'd be recuperating if I'd taken those signs seriously.
point: 過去の仮定から今の回復を表す、convalesce は病後回復する。

ja: 痛くなったら電話するよ。
en: I'll call if it hurts.
alternatives: I'll phone you if it hurts.
If it hurts, I'll call you.
point: 未来のことでも if 節は現在形

ja: 数週間ずっと肩がこってる。
en: I've had stiff shoulders for weeks.
alternatives: My shoulders have been stiff for weeks.
I've had tight shoulders for weeks.
point: for + 期間の継続は現在完了

ja: 食べたものが胃にもたれてる気がする。
en: I think what I ate isn't sitting well.
alternatives: I think what I ate disagrees with me.
I think something I ate disagrees with me.
point: isn't sitting well は胃にもたれるの定番表現

ja: 朝食を抜いて、めまいがした。
en: Having skipped breakfast, I felt faint.
alternatives: Since I'd skipped breakfast, I felt faint.
I felt faint because I'd skipped breakfast.
point: 先に起きたことは Having + 過去分詞

ja: 病院で血圧を測ってもらったよ。
en: I had my blood pressure taken.
alternatives: I got my blood pressure checked.
I had my blood pressure checked.
point: 測ってもらうは have + 物 + 過去分詞

ja: 近くに薬局があるよ。
en: There's a pharmacy nearby.
alternatives: A pharmacy is nearby.
There's a drugstore nearby.
point: 「〜がある」は There's + 単数の名詞

ja: 私、元気そうでも気力は底だ。
en: Though outwardly chipper, I'm running on fumes.
alternatives: I seem cheerful, though I'm completely spent.
Despite looking upbeat, I'm barely keeping going.
point: chipper は快活な、run on fumes は気力が尽きかけた状態。

ja: 私、よく眠れた。
en: I slept well.
alternatives: I had a good sleep.
I slept soundly.
point: slept は sleep の過去形。

ja: どこが痛みますか？
en: Where does it hurt?
alternatives: Where is the pain?
Where do you feel pain?
point: 「痛む」は hurt。疑問詞＋ does it

ja: 息子が咳き込んでる。
en: My son is coughing.
alternatives: My son is coughing hard.
My son keeps coughing.
point: 今起きていることは be + -ing

ja: 君は彼からうつされたに違いない。
en: You must have caught it from him.
alternatives: You must have picked it up from him.
You must have gotten it from him.
point: 過去への確信は must have + 過去分詞

ja: 休んでれば、今ごろ回復してるのに。
en: If I'd rested, I'd be better by now.
alternatives: If I'd rested, I'd be on the mend now.
If I had rested, I'd be better by now.
point: 過去の if 節と今の結果：would be。better by now は「今ごろは回復」

ja: 予約、明日に変えられますか？
en: Can I reschedule for tomorrow?
alternatives: Could I move my appointment to tomorrow?
Can I change it to tomorrow?
point: 予約の変更は reschedule / move が定番

ja: 休むように言われたよ。
en: I was told to rest.
alternatives: They told me to rest.
I was advised to rest.
point: 「言われた」は be told + to + 動詞

ja: 医者に休養が必要だと言われた。
en: The doctor said I needed rest.
alternatives: The doctor told me I needed rest.
My doctor said I needed to rest.
point: said の後は need も過去形に

ja: この頭痛、早く治まってほしいな。
en: I wish this headache would go away.
alternatives: If only this headache would go away.
I wish this headache would just go away.
I hope this headache goes away soon.
point: 今への不満や願いは wish + would

ja: 私の症状は一度も和らがなかった。
en: Never once did my symptoms let up.
alternatives: My symptoms never eased up.
My symptoms never subsided.
point: let up は症状や強さが和らぐこと。

ja: 家に帰ったら休むよ。
en: I'll rest once I'm home.
alternatives: I'll rest when I get home.
When I get home, I'll rest.
point: 未来のことでも when / once 節は現在形

ja: 薬局はもう閉まってた。
en: The pharmacy had already closed.
alternatives: The pharmacy was already closed.
The pharmacy had closed by then.
point: 過去のある時点より前は had ＋ 過去分詞

ja: 私は忍耐と健康を混同してるかも。
en: I may be conflating fortitude with wellness.
alternatives: I might be confusing mental toughness with good health.
I may be mistaking endurance for being healthy.
point: fortitude は苦痛に耐える強さ、健康そのものとは区別する。

ja: 休んでたら、再発しなかったのに。
en: If I'd rested, I wouldn't have relapsed.
alternatives: If I'd taken it easy, I wouldn't have relapsed.
Had I rested, I wouldn't have relapsed.
point: 病気の「ぶり返す」は relapse

ja: 今日は休んだほうがいいよ。
en: You should rest today.
alternatives: You'd better rest today.
You should take today off.
point: アドバイスは should

ja: 水をたくさん飲んで。
en: Drink lots of water.
alternatives: Drink plenty of water.
Drink a lot of water.
point: water は数えられない。lots of を使う

ja: 医者に診てもらうよ。
en: I'll see a doctor.
alternatives: I'm going to see a doctor.
I'll go see a doctor.
point: 「診てもらう」は see a doctor

ja: 彼は私の症状は軽いと言った。
en: He said my symptoms are mild.
alternatives: He told me my symptoms were mild.
He said my condition is minor.
point: said の後でも、今も本当なら現在形でよい

ja: 昨日、熱が出たんだ。
en: I had a fever yesterday.
alternatives: I got a fever yesterday.
I ran a fever yesterday.
point: 熱が「ある・出る」は have / get a fever

ja: 三日間ずっと咳が出てる。
en: I've been coughing for three days.
alternatives: I've had a cough for three days.
I've been coughing nonstop for three days.
point: 今も続く動作は have been ＋ -ing

ja: 私は水を飲む必要がある。
en: I need to drink water.
alternatives: I have to drink water.
I must drink some water.
point: need to + 動詞で必要な行動を伝える。

ja: たっぷり寝たのに、ぐったりだ。
en: Despite a full night's sleep, I'm wiped out.
alternatives: Even though I slept well, I'm wiped out.
Although I slept well, I'm wiped out.
point: Despite の後は名詞。「ぐったり」は wiped out

ja: 私の足が震えてる。
en: My legs are shaking.
alternatives: My legs are trembling.
My legs are shaky.
point: are shaking で今震えていると伝える。

ja: 風邪をひきかけてるんだ。
en: I'm coming down with a cold.
alternatives: I think I'm catching a cold.
I feel a cold coming on.
point: 「かかりかけ」は come down with

ja: 今日は具合が悪いんだ。
en: I'm sick today.
alternatives: I'm not feeling well.
I don't feel well today.
point: 「具合が悪い」は I'm sick

ja: 水が必要です。
en: I need water.
alternatives: I need some water.
Water is what I need.
point: water は数えないので a をつけない。

ja: 私は小康を回復と誤解したはず。
en: I must've confused respite with recovery.
alternatives: I must have mistaken temporary relief for recovery.
I must've taken a brief improvement for recovery.
point: respite は一時の休息や軽快、recovery は回復。

ja: もっと早く病院に行けばよかった。
en: I wish I'd seen a doctor sooner.
alternatives: If only I'd seen a doctor sooner.
I should have seen a doctor sooner.
point: 「医者にかかる」は see a doctor
